## Constraints

### Every command in the WinSafe window claims a distinct Alt key

`proposed` · `@evidence-intake-project.constraint.distinct-alt-keys/1` · scope `path "src/gui/winsafe.rs"`

No two controls in the WinSafe main window may claim the same mnemonic letter. Win32 resolves a mnemonic across the whole window, so a repeated letter makes Alt cycle focus between the claimants instead of pressing either one -- which silently breaks the keyboard path the status bar advertises, without any visible symptom. Command captions therefore live as named constants at the top of src/gui/winsafe.rs, and the unit test every_command_has_its_own_alt_key is what keeps them distinct.

- `#labels-claim-mnemonics-too` — A static label takes the same ampersand prefix as a button, so a heading may not contain a bare ampersand. The heading 'COLLATION & EXPORT' would have claimed Alt+Space, which is the system menu.
- `#what-the-collisions-were` — Before this pass four commands claimed Alt+V -- Seed Vehicle, Save Export, Reviewed and Verify -- and further pairs collided on O, R, T, S and I. Fixing them forced several captions to change: the import command became 'Import Normalized Batch' and the authoring command became 'Save New Record', both of which are also more accurate than what they replaced.

### The DPI-scaled window is clamped to the screen and floored at a size the layout survives

`proposed` · `@evidence-intake-project.constraint.window-fits-the-screen/1` · scope `path "src/gui/winsafe.rs"`

The WinSafe layout is written in logical units and gui::dpi scales every coordinate by the system DPI, so the window grows with the user's display scaling: the 1100x700 design size wants 1650x1050 device pixels at 150% and 2200x1400 at 200%. Windows will create a window larger than the screen, which puts the bottom command row past the edge with no way to reach it, so fit_to_work_area shrinks the window onto the monitor's work area at WM_CREATE. It never shrinks below the layout's floor of 940x600 logical, which WM_GETMINMAXINFO also enforces as the minimum tracking size: a window that overflows can still be moved to reach the rest of it, whereas one shrunk past the floor has commands that overlap and cannot be separated again.

- `#labels-shrink-rather-than-collide` — A label whose right edge would run under a right-anchored control is given Horz::Resize rather than a fixed width, so the gap between them is preserved as the window narrows. Every label carries SS_ENDELLIPSIS so the text it loses ends in an ellipsis instead of a stroke cut mid-glyph.
- `#the-bottom-row-sets-the-width-floor` — MIN_WIDTH is set by the bottom command row: Reject ends at a fixed logical 592 while the authoring pair is right-anchored and slides left as the window narrows, so the two collide once the window loses about 190 logical units.
- `#the-rail-sets-the-height-floor` — MIN_HEIGHT is set by the navigation rail, not by the output pane. The rail is anchored and does not move on resize, so its last button's lower edge at logical 578 is the floor; a height derived from the output pane instead was measured at 470 and hid the four collation and export commands off the bottom of the window.

### The video adapter never emits speed, identity, speaker-to-face matching, enhancement, authenticity, redaction or reconstruction

`proposed` · `@evidence-intake-project.video.no-forensic-assertions/1` · scope `path "adapters/video/**"`

No extractor in the video adapter, and no analyzer in the kernel fed by it, produces any of the following, in any state including suggested: a vehicle speed or distance; an identification of a person, vehicle plate or object with a named entity (by face, gait, voice, clothing or any other feature); a match between a diarized speaker and a figure in frame; an enhanced, stabilized, upscaled or otherwise altered rendition presented as evidence; a judgement of authenticity, tampering or editing; a redacted derivative; or a 3D, pose or depth reconstruction (LingBot-Map class). Where such an analysis matters to a case it is a retained expert's work product, entered by a person through authoring with a rationale, never an adapter output.

- `#no-altered-rendition` — The adapter derives stills and indexes from the original but never emits an enhanced, redacted or reconstructed rendition as a source.
- `#no-identity` — No adapter output names a person or matches a speaker to a figure in frame; linking a track, speaker or detection to an entity is always an authored edge with a written rationale.
- `#no-measurement` — No adapter output states a speed, distance or authenticity judgement.

**derived_from** `@evidence-intake-project.decision.video-intake-points-never-asserts/1`

### cuda-local-vlm-video-captioning is a useful benchmark reference, not a drop-in adapter

`verified` · `@evidence-intake-project.video.cuda-local-vlm-captioning-fit/2`

Inspection of ssheld/cuda-local-vlm-video-captioning at its sole initial public commit 3a354b5c5e44a55817f53a95182006b508ddeaff found a useful MIT-licensed alpha reference for load-once CUDA VLM runtimes, model-family adapters, browser smoke gates, structured JSONL provenance, and latency/peak-VRAM comparison. It is not a drop-in video intake module: its batch CLI uniformly samples a fixed count over the whole MP4 with OpenCV, deletes temporary frames, records a local path rather than an original hash and interval locator, follows unpinned model ids by default with trust_remote_code, and its animal-oriented schema asks for behavior, interaction and count fields that do not fit the project's point-never-assert contract. Reuse the runtime and benchmark patterns while retaining this project's bounded scene sampler, original-timeline locators, conservative suggested captions and pinned offline artifacts.

### lege-gpu is a useful native GPU foundation but not a drop-in SigLIP2 runtime

`verified` · `@evidence-intake-project.video.lege-gpu-siglip2-fit/2` · scope `path "Cargo.lock"`, `path "Cargo.toml"`, `path "adapters/video/**"`

Inspection of the clean lege-gpu source tree at sibling repository HEAD 3f520cc03211e48adaa77c1da9bc639c53d2d351 found a custom ONNX-to-wgpu document-vision runtime whose generic session accepts a hard-coded set of single FLOAT image inputs, represents runtime tensors only as f32, lacks SigLIP2 transformer requirements such as LayerNormalization/GELU and runtime integer token gathering, and recompiles the generic graph on every run_gpu call. A local hardware-policy test did successfully select the NVIDIA RTX 4060 Laptop GPU through DX12. lege-gpu can contribute proven adapter selection, resident-buffer planning, and wgpu kernels to a future native backend, but using it for SigLIP2 would first require model export, typed multi-input tensors, transformer operator lowering, tokenization/preprocessing, a persistent batched session, and parity/performance tests; it cannot replace the current PyTorch benchmark backend now.

- `#native-potential` — The RTX 4060 DX12 selection test and existing wgpu runtime make lege-gpu a credible foundation only if a separately scoped transformer-runtime extension is justified by the retrieval benchmark.
- `#not-drop-in` — The current lege-gpu public session cannot load or execute the downloaded SigLIP2 checkpoint as a drop-in backend.

**supersedes** `@evidence-intake-project.video.lege-gpu-siglip2-fit/1` · **derived_from** `@evidence-intake-project.video.real-embedding-benchmark/1`

### Pinned Qwen2-VL supports a conservative load-once visual skim index

`verified` · `@evidence-intake-project.video.qwen2-vl-donetsk-caption-smoke/3`

The replacement evidence sample jaf69w.mp4 (SHA-256 E92C56F7BD9E53B98866D1D79BC61358F0257C62409E29477D3A23D751B41140) fully decoded as 13:54.781 of 1280x720 H.264 at 25 fps with AAC audio. In an isolated Transformers 5.7.0 environment sharing torch 2.13.0+cu132, the Apache-2.0 Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct checkpoint pinned at 895c3a49bc3fa70a340399125c650a463535e71c loaded from two verified local weight shards totaling 4.13 GiB. A four-frame joint request completed in 44.6 seconds but peaked at 7469.5 MiB CUDA allocation on the 8 GiB RTX 4060; keeping the model resident and captioning 24 frames independently completed in 75.998 seconds and peaked at 4568.8 MiB. The integrated project-owned Rust-to-Python batch backend then processed 26 scene windows across the first 02:00.040 in one load-once process. It stored 26 suggested observations using only a deterministic bounded visible-feature vocabulary, stamped every caption with the pinned model revision, retained no free-form model prose, and produced zero matches for military, police, officer, firefighter, patient, riot, protest, attack, explosion, guilty or innocent. The 00:39.480-00:44.480 window is indexed as multiple people, camouflage clothing, vehicle, building and road, preserving directly visible appearance without assigning a military role. The adapter supports explicit null abstention, although this sample produced none. Qwen2-VL is therefore usable as a suggested visual skim index when run sequentially with a resident offline model, deterministic output reduction and human review; it is not a factual narrator and must not provide identity, role, event or legal conclusions.

**depends_on** `@evidence-intake-project.decision.video-intake-points-never-asserts/1` · **supersedes** `@evidence-intake-project.video.qwen2-vl-donetsk-caption-smoke/2` · **derived_from** `@evidence-intake-project.video.real-embedding-benchmark/1`

### Scene-only sampling leaves long unrepresented spans in the local video sample

`verified` · `@evidence-intake-project.video.sample-scene-coverage-gap/3` · scope `path "adapters/video/**"`

Against the current local 18:34.986 H.264 sample, ffmpeg scene scoring at the adapter default 0.30 threshold produced 57 cuts (58 scenes). The median interval was 8.74 seconds, 15 intervals exceeded 30 seconds, 6 exceeded 60 seconds, and the maximum was 76.94 seconds. Because the adapter extracts only the frame at each scene start, the visual finder cannot retrieve anything visible only between those sampled instants.

**supersedes** `@evidence-intake-project.video.sample-scene-coverage-gap/2` · **derived_from** `@evidence-intake-project.video.scene-core/1`

### The synthetic 0.20 cosine cut returns no SigLIP 2 candidates on the local sample

`verified` · `@evidence-intake-project.video.siglip2-cut-distribution/4` · scope `path "adapters/video/**"`, `path "src/store.rs"`, `path "src/views.rs"`

The local google/siglip2-base-patch16-384 checkpoint embedded 254 hybrid-sampled frames from the 18:34.986 local video into finite normalized 768-dimensional vectors. Across nine representative text queries, maximum cosine similarity ranged from 0.0766 to 0.1204 and zero frames met the synthetic KEYFRAME_SIMILARITY_CUT of 0.20. The fixed cut therefore makes the live visual finder return no candidates even though the model produces a usable relative ordering.

### SigLIP2 abstains on standalone labels for the first two minutes of DVIDS 966833

`verified` · `@evidence-intake-project.video.siglip2-standalone-label-abstention-dvids-966833/3`

The highest-quality official DVIDS 966833 rendition (SHA-256 97F3FA71E8AC5572081837E7F778D2DD8AFB22B8E694C313F0D0B39578A925F0) was fully decoded and hybrid-sampled into 26 frames in [0,120000) ms. With the local google/siglip2-base-patch16-384 checkpoint, five neutral label groups, three paraphrases per label, the checkpoint's learned cosine scale and bias, and an availability rule requiring every paraphrase both to clear the native 0.5 sigmoid threshold and choose the same label, zero labels were available in every group on all 26 frames. Only five added-text prompt decisions and one vehicle prompt decision individually cleared 0.5; setting, people and view-quality had none. A forced-choice comparison had only 0-19.2% paraphrase agreement and zero vehicle agreement. This checkpoint therefore did not produce responsible standalone text identifications for this window and vocabulary, although the result does not disqualify it as a relative text-to-frame retrieval encoder.

**supersedes** `@evidence-intake-project.video.siglip2-standalone-label-abstention-dvids-966833/2` · **derived_from** `@evidence-intake-project.video.real-embedding-benchmark/1`

## Assessments

### Mapping stays collation only while it presents sourced placement rather than deriving forensic opinions

`verified` · `@evidence-intake-project.assessment.mapping-boundary-follows-software-output/1`

The meaningful scope boundary follows what the software derives and claims, not whether its operator is a public defender. A map remains a collation read model when it plots only source-stated or reviewer-confirmed locations, preserves raw location language, provenance, exact locators and disagreement, labels address-to-coordinate conversion as derived and reviewable, and returns the reviewer to the underlying document, audio or video. It crosses the adopted forensic boundary when it authenticates media, infers location from pixels, measures depicted objects or distances, compares scenes or people to render an identification opinion, reconstructs routes or events, or asserts a common event across sources.

- `#forensic-crossing` — Image-derived geolocation or measurement, authentication, comparative identification and route or event reconstruction cross the adopted product boundary.
- `#role-is-not-boundary` — A defender reviewing evidence is doing litigation analysis, but the user's role does not make every review action a technical forensic examination.
- `#safe-map` — A safe map is a provenance-preserving read model over source-stated or reviewer-confirmed location anchors.
